reference_sections.heading: Applicable resources and claim boundaries
reference_sections.text:
| Reference | What we can study | What it cannot establish |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [R02](../RESOURCES.md#r02), [R03](../RESOURCES.md#r03) | Published F-22 HUD illustration; R03 Figure 3 reproduces the earlier USAF illustration. Basic layout and the discussion of counter-pointer presentation are relevant. | Two independent cockpit captures, every tactical mode, current software-tape behavior or installed angular dimensions. R02 direct access is blocked. |
| [R01](../RESOURCES.md#r01) | Dated manufacturer HUD rig footage. Retain only as corroborating historical material. | An operational flight recording or sufficient sole reference. The user rejected this video as the principal reference. |
| [R06–R09](../RESOURCES.md#r06), [R88](../RESOURCES.md#r88) | Cockpit/display architecture and HUD modernization context. | A full symbol dictionary. Generic projector field-of-view/resolution specifications are not the installed aircraft's optical calibration. |
| [R12](../RESOURCES.md#r12), [R91](../RESOURCES.md#r91), [R99](../RESOURCES.md#r99) | Evaluation methods, dynamics/latency and USAF symbology human factors. | F-22-specific shapes, warning criteria or mode priorities. R91 concerns another aircraft/simulator. |
| [R156–R158](../RESOURCES.md#r156) | Chinese studies of character readability, workload and civil conformal flight guidance. | Raptor symbology. The general-aviation study used a Cessna-based simulator; CAAC material concerns civil HUD use. |
| [R51](../RESOURCES.md#r51), [R125](../RESOURCES.md#r125) | Investigation reconstructions and pilot systems context. | Literal HUD-camera evidence. Reconstructed flight views must not be traced as exact symbols. |

No verified public real-aircraft F-22 flight manual or comprehensive HUD mode/symbol handbook was located in this search. This is a search result, not proof that no further public material exists. Simulator manuals and unverified uploads are excluded from aircraft-authenticity claims.

The later [forum follow-up](../CHINESE_FORUM_RESEARCH.md#hud-and-manual-traps-encountered) screened additional image, video and manual leads. It did not establish a new authenticated tactical-symbol set; [the addendum](RESEARCH_ADDENDUM.md) preserves that evidence boundary.

### Visible cues to preserve from R03 Figure 3

| Observation | Reconstruction boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Left/right circular counter-pointer speed/altitude presentation | Do not substitute inherited vertical tapes. |
| Solid positive and dashed negative pitch marks | Exact angular spacing/declutter needs calibration. |
| Distinct central circular/winged and W-shaped cues; lower curved tick arc | Record shapes separately; cue semantics/mode behavior require corroboration. |

This is an illustration, not a calibrated combiner photograph.

reference_sections.heading: Source-review coverage and limits
reference_sections.text:
Baseline: [`9c5d03ee822323591dbf259d09b5022ced3e3d4f`](https://github.com/Ethanw05/DCS-F22/tree/9c5d03ee822323591dbf259d09b5022ced3e3d4f); 24 October 2026. Source links below are pinned to that baseline. Documentation changes do not alter the reviewed aircraft code.

## Inventory and methods

The inventory contains **132 tracked source/configuration files, 46,267 lines**: Lua/SDEF, C++/headers, JSON, workflow YAML and CMake files. All **117 Lua/SDEF** files passed Lua **5.1.5** syntax checking (only a leading UTF-8 BOM was stripped for parsing). There are **38 display page scripts**, all constructed under minimal substitutes for common DCS drawing helpers. Their checked controller parameter indices were in bounds and no repeated insertion of the same object was detected. This is not a DCS rendering test.

The central EFM and active system flows received semantic/state review. Repeated declarative pages and asset descriptors were reviewed through structure, comparisons and references. This is a full **file-coverage source assessment**, not a claim of branch-complete execution or independent verification of every undocumented DCS field. The ABI headers were inspected as contracts, rather than treated as aircraft algorithms to change.

Seven active Lua devices were loaded with synthetic host functions; selected power, trigger, hydraulic and brake paths were exercised. Extracted unchanged C++ callbacks used actual baseline state/helpers with a no-op cockpit bridge. They reproduced selected continuity, trim, repair/reset and event results. Earlier fuel and actuator experiments remain documented against unchanged code. Temporary analysis programs are outside this repository; no audit tools are added.

## What was not validated

- No installed Windows DCS runtime, full Windows DLL build, native guided engagement, clean FC-disabled boot, multiplayer/track replay, VR or rendered cockpit validation.
- No access to proprietary inherited F-15C avionics source, which supplies behavior absent from this tree.
- Compiled EDMs, DLL binaries, textures, audio and mission archives were inventoried as assets, not reverse engineered or flight-tested. No complete original 3D authoring project was located.
- No real aircraft, production F119 deck, complete aerodynamic database, operational software tape or authenticated complete HUD manual was obtained.

License/attribution and existing project documentation were also considered for distribution and provenance; they are not counted as aircraft source files below. A file mapped to a review without a defect means the checked scope produced no specific confirmed defect, not that the file is proven correct.

reference_sections.heading: Reviewed source behavior
reference_sections.text:
- `Defensive_Overview.lua` uses current radar-backed track range when available. Passive-only observations stay on a fixed outer bearing ring; their payload cannot manufacture radar range. Invalid scale suppresses a measured-position presentation. Pitch/bank are removed for a level heading-up bearing picture.
- RF launch/lock and optical warning freshness use their own observation timestamps. Fresh radar range does not renew old RF or optical warning evidence; fresh RF does not renew expired radar range. Explicit friendly/unknown/hostile affiliation is passed through, rather than inferred from sensor type.
- The publisher bounds output to 16 plottable records, prioritizes selected/urgent evidence, reports overflow, and clears records on power/invalid-frame loss. A vertical ray with no horizontal bearing is rejected before allocating/counting a display slot.
- Actual native format construction verifies all bound overview fields exist, element names are unique, parents resolve, line materials exist and affiliation/alert branches have visible colors. The MFD independently expires the picture after 0.25 model seconds, rejecting future stamps and hiding the last threat symbols after a producer stall.
- Overview exposes MENU, DETAIL and ALL/THRT. Hidden detail/editor keys are consumed. Actual RWR/EW/MFD tests exercise DETAIL entry/exit, a held CM-editor command, release after returning to overview, the next accepted editor press and parent MENU routing.

reference_sections.heading: AER-01 - Reconcile reference geometry and validate performance by configuration
reference_sections.text:
**Priority/type:** P2 / C/I.

**Implementation:** [EFM/source/RAPTOR.h](<C:/Users/Ethans Desktop 2.0/Documents/Codex/2026-10-24/o/outputs/DCS-F22/EFM/source/RAPTOR.h:88>); [F-22A.lua](<C:/Users/Ethans Desktop 2.0/Documents/Codex/2026-10-24/o/outputs/DCS-F22/F-22A.lua:104>); [EFM/source/RAPTOR.h](<C:/Users/Ethans Desktop 2.0/Documents/Codex/2026-10-24/o/outputs/DCS-F22/EFM/source/RAPTOR.h:32>).

**Finding:** The EFM reference area is 78.06 m2 while the aircraft Lua table says 56.5 m2. This is a configuration inconsistency; it does not mean the Lua value directly sets player EFM forces. Coefficients and reference areas must be considered together.

**Fix/improvement:** Document the chosen geometry/reference convention and reconcile AI/player configuration intentionally. Build conditioned performance cases for weight, altitude, stores and power. Public CFD pictures with missing scales cannot supply replacement coefficients.

**Acceptance:** Check level-flight thrust/drag balance, acceleration, climb, turn and approach at recorded mass/configuration. Compare only to sources with compatible conditions, with declared uncertainty.

**Resources:** [S05](https://www.cobaltcfd.com/pdfs/AIAA_2013_ratcliff.pdf), [S06](https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20000115606), [S07](https://www.rtx.com/prattwhitney/products/military-engines/f119), [S32](https://www.af.mil/About-Us/Fact-Sheets/Display/Article/104506/f-22-raptor/About-Us/f-22-raptor/).

reference_sections.heading: Resource register
reference_sections.text:
Source IDs in each finding resolve to the entries below. Exact paper titles, access depth and useful limits are included so another contributor can verify the claim without repeating the whole search.


### S01 - [Ronald W. Brower, USAF: Lockheed F-22 Raptor, The Avionics Handbook, chapter 32 (2001)](https://www.helitavia.com/avionics/TheAvionicsHandbook_Cap_32.pdf)

**Reviewed/access:** Relevant full sections read; PDF downloaded.

**Use and limit:** Sections 32.2, 32.3.2-32.3.7 and 32.4: fusion, sensor roles, displays, CNI, EW, stores and reconfiguration. Historical architecture, not a current operating manual.


### S02 - [National Museum of the USAF: F-22A cockpit, VIRIN 080116-F-1234P-002](https://www.nationalmuseum.af.mil/Upcoming/Photos/igphoto/2000412735/)

**Reviewed/access:** Official catalog/provenance previously checked; image and user crops inspected. Catalog returned 403 during this pass.

**Use and limit:** Front-view bay schematic and combined lower status display. Exact USAF photograph also preserved through the Wikimedia mirror; museum imagery does not establish an operational software tape.


### S03 - [Lt Col Randy Gordon: F-22 Flight Controls, MIT OpenCourseWare](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/16-687-private-pilot-ground-school-january-iap-2019/resources/special-lecture-f-22-flight-controls/)

**Reviewed/access:** Course record and seven-page slides read; PDF pages 3-5 visually inspected. Video not watched in this pass.

**Use and limit:** FCS synoptic, landing/refueling modes, limiters and pilot-command concepts. Course labeled IAP 2019; slides carry 1/30/20. Teaching material, no production gains.


### S04 - [Harris and Black: F-22 Control Law Development and Flying Qualities, AIAA 96-3379 (1996)](https://doi.org/10.2514/6.1996-3379)

**Reviewed/access:** Author-posted full-text mirror read through web; local download blocked.

**Use and limit:** Especially printed pp. 5-8: F-22 design goals, mode-transition consistency and nonlinear/PIO evaluation. Earlier YF-22 material is explicitly prototype evidence.


### S05 - [Clifton, Ratcliff, Bodkin and Dean, USAF SEEK EAGLE: high-resolution CFD and stability/control (2013)](https://www.cobaltcfd.com/pdfs/AIAA_2013_ratcliff.pdf)

**Reviewed/access:** PDF downloaded; relevant results text read; page 5 visually inspected.

**Use and limit:** Static/dynamic validation and clean/external-tank configuration comparisons. Public plots intentionally withhold absolute aerodynamic data; cannot recover an F-22 coefficient deck.


### S06 - [Joseph Chambers: Partners in Freedom, NASA/SP-2000-4519](https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20000115606)

**Reviewed/access:** NASA PDF downloaded; F-22 chapter, printed pp. 159-165 / PDF pp. 172-178 read.

**Use and limit:** Historical nozzle/afterbody, high-alpha and supersonic-drag development. Its specification box is historical, not a modern weight/performance schedule.


### S07 - [Pratt & Whitney: F119 engine](https://www.rtx.com/prattwhitney/products/military-engines/f119)

**Reviewed/access:** Manufacturer technical page read.

**Use and limit:** Twin-spool augmented engine, 35,000-lb thrust class, pitch vectoring up to 20 degrees and integrated FADEC. Does not provide an installed thrust/fuel/transient deck.


### S08 - [Northrop Grumman: AN/APG-77 AESA radar](https://www.northropgrumman.com/what-we-do/mission-solutions/radars/an-apg-77-aesa)

**Reviewed/access:** Manufacturer page read.

**Use and limit:** Electronic beam agility and multiple-target engagement architecture. No verified detection ranges, scan schedules, probability-of-detection or LPI immunity figures.


### S09 - [Boeing: Begins Integrating F-22 Fighter's Advanced Avionics (1998)](https://boeing.mediaroom.com/1998-01-29-Boeing-Begins-Integrating-F-22-Fighters-Advanced-Avionics)

**Reviewed/access:** Manufacturer article body read.

**Use and limit:** Integration of vehicle, stores, controls, track fusion and navigation; supports coherent ownership and integrated testing, not exact UI geometry.


### S10 - [Air Force Reserve: Combat Hammer/Archer and Increment 3.1 (2013)](https://www.afrc.af.mil/News/Article-Display/Article/156442/projecting-capability-alaska-f-22s-drop-in-on-combat-hammer-archer/)

**Reviewed/access:** Official indexed excerpt checked; article body blocked with 403.

**Use and limit:** Confirms operational use of upgraded SAR ground mapping. Limited to the indexed capability statement; no inference of exact GMTI performance or page controls.


### S11 - [DOT&E FY2018 Annual Report, F-22A section](https://www.dote.osd.mil/Portals/97/pub/reports/FY2018/other/2018DOTEAnnualReport.pdf?ver=2019-08-21-155621-540)

**Reviewed/access:** Official indexed F-22 excerpts checked; full PDF retrieval blocked.

**Use and limit:** Increment 3.1 SAR/surface designation and SDB context; 3.2B development/fielding context. Not read as a complete operational test report.


### S12 - [Lockheed Martin: F-22 Infrared Defensive System integration contract (22 January 2025)](https://news.lockheedmartin.com/2025-01-22-Lockheed-Martin-to-Modernize-Air-Force-F-22-Raptor-with-Advanced-Infrared-Threat-Detection-Sensors)

**Reviewed/access:** Manufacturer announcement text checked.

**Use and limit:** Embedded TacIRST/IRDS modernization is a credible extension. Contract/integration announcement is not proof of fleet-wide fielding or an EO/IR targeting-pod interface.


### S13 - [Lockheed Martin: Project Hydra, F-22/F-35/U-2 communications demonstration (2021)](https://news.lockheedmartin.com/lockheed-martin-skunk-work-project-hydra-demonstrates-5th-gen-to-5th-gen-communications-across-domains?asPDF=1)

**Reviewed/access:** Complete one-page manufacturer release read.

**Use and limit:** IFDL/MADL gateway demonstration and exchanged tracks. Does not establish universal direct F-22/F-35 interoperability on every aircraft.


### S14 - [Eagle Dynamics: DCS F/A-18C Early Access Guide EN](https://www.digitalcombatsimulator.com/en/downloads/documentation/dcs-fa-18c_early_access_guide_en/)

**Reviewed/access:** Installed 424-page official manual used; relevant pages 186-198, 204-206, 303-306 read; stores diagram visually inspected.

**Use and limit:** Simulation comparison: radar MAP/EXP/GMT, SA, SMS wingform, modes, fuzes and UFC programming. Authoritative for ED Hornet behavior, not the F-22.


### S15 - [Eagle Dynamics: DCS F-16C Early Access Guide EN, updated 16 August 2026](https://www.digitalcombatsimulator.com/en/downloads/documentation/dcs-viper_early_access_manual_en/)

**Reviewed/access:** Local 774-page official guide used; relevant pages 358-360, 366, 619-623 read; key SMS pages visually inspected.

**Use and limit:** Simulation comparison: HSD, inventory versus employment, retained profiles and MFD numerical entry. Does not justify calling our keypad workflow an authentic F-16/F-22 procedure.


### S16 - [Kiyohiko Aiba: HUD moving-tape versus counter-pointer survey, JASDF Aeromedical Laboratory 48(1), 21-29 (2008)](https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/jasdfaml/48/1/48_21/_pdf/-char/ja)

**Reviewed/access:** Public full-text article read through web; abstract, methods and Fig. 3 context checked.

**Use and limit:** Historical F-22 counter-pointer illustration; survey of 160 JASDF pilots. Preference survey, not a flight-performance experiment or current F-22 HUD dimensional specification.


### S17 - [USAF Flying Safety, June 2002, HUD airspeed/altitude article](https://www.safety.af.mil/Portals/71/documents/Magazines/FSM/fsmjun02.pdf?ver=2017-03-28-101049-403)

**Reviewed/access:** Indexed official article text checked; PDF download blocked.

**Use and limit:** Historical counter-pointer provenance. Aiba reuses its F-22 illustration, so these do not constitute two independent cockpit captures.


### S18 - [Letlow and Jenkins: Development of an Integrated Environmental Control System, SAE 981544 (1998)](https://doi.org/10.4271/981544)

**Reviewed/access:** Publisher abstract read; full paper not obtained.

**Use and limit:** ECS/TMS coupling, digital control and fuel as a heat sink. Supports architecture only, not hydraulic/thermal calibration.


### S19 - [Sprouse: F-22 ECS/TMS Design Optimization for Reliability and Integrity, SAE 961339 (1996)](https://doi.org/10.4271/961339)

**Reviewed/access:** Publisher abstract read; full paper not obtained.

**Use and limit:** Integrated thermal conditioning/pressurization and reliability scope. No detailed failure probabilities or operating limits recovered.


### S20 - [Ghanekar: Vapor Cycle System for the F-22 Raptor, SAE 2000-01-2268](https://doi.org/10.4271/2000-01-2268)

**Reviewed/access:** Publisher abstract read; full paper not obtained.

**Use and limit:** Variable-speed vapor-cycle electronics cooling. Confirms a system absent from the present physical model; does not publish a usable heat-rejection map here.


### S21 - [Ashford and Brown: ECS/TMS Flight Test Program - Downloadable Constants, SAE 2000-01-2265](https://doi.org/10.4271/2000-01-2265)

**Reviewed/access:** Publisher abstract read; full paper not obtained.

**Use and limit:** Transient flight conditions exposed issues not predicted by steady-state/ground tests. Useful validation rationale, not a calibration dataset.


### S22 - [Ashford: Verification and Validation of F/A-22 ECS/TMS Software, SAE 2004-01-2573](https://doi.org/10.4271/2004-01-2573)

**Reviewed/access:** Publisher abstract read; full paper not obtained.

**Use and limit:** Staged software qualification culminating in flight test. Process reference, not evidence that this mod passes comparable certification.


### S23 - [Sandia National Laboratories: What is Synthetic Aperture Radar?](https://www.sandia.gov/radar/pathfinder-radar-isr-and-synthetic-aperture-radar-sar-systems/what-is-sar/)

**Reviewed/access:** Technical explanatory article read.

**Use and limit:** Range/azimuth image formation and resolution. Supports the distinction between a radar image and scattered points; not APG-77 implementation data.


### S24 - [Armin Doerry: GMTI Processing using Back Projection, SAND2013-5111](https://www.sandia.gov/research/publications/details/gmti-processing-using-back-projection-2013-07-01/)

**Reviewed/access:** Laboratory abstract and DOI 10.2172/1090227 checked; full report not retrieved.

**Use and limit:** GMTI range/velocity processing and migration. Method lead only; no F-22-specific modes or minimum detectable speeds established.


### S25 - [General Dynamics Ordnance and Tactical Systems: F-22A M61A2 gun system](https://www.gdots.com/armaments/aircraft-guns-gun-systems/f22/)

**Reviewed/access:** Manufacturer specifications read.

**Use and limit:** 480 rounds, 6,000 shots/minute, hydraulic drive. Page title and metric weight conversions contain inconsistencies; do not import its weight column without an independent check.


### S26 - [NAVAIR: Direct Attack Weapons](https://www.navair.navy.mil/product/Direct-Attack-Weapons)

**Reviewed/access:** Official technical text read.

**Use and limit:** GP bombs, GPS/INS JDAM, laser JDAM and fuze-function distinctions. Moving-target sensing alone does not convert a coordinate-only bomb into a mover-capable weapon.


### S27 - [Lockheed Martin: Mako, a Hypersonic Missile That's More Than Ready (2024)](https://www.lockheedmartin.com/en-us/news/features/2024/mako-a-hypersonic-missile-thats-more-than-ready.html)

**Reviewed/access:** Manufacturer indexed excerpt checked; page body blocked with 403.

**Use and limit:** Internal F-22 physical fit check supports plausibility of an extension. Does not prove flight clearance, service entry, or the mod's seeker/range/warhead values.


### S28 - [Bundled Eagle Dynamics external-flight-model interface contract](<C:/Users/Ethans Desktop 2.0/Documents/Codex/2026-10-24/o/outputs/DCS-F22/EFM/include/FM/wHumanCustomPhysicsAPI.h:404>)

**Reviewed/access:** Current local header read, especially engine parameter definitions and mass callbacks.

**Use and limit:** Implementation interface evidence: RPM versus related RPM, force/fuel/mass semantics. Not real-aircraft performance evidence; verify against the supported DCS build.


### S29 - [Rainey and Kohn: F-22 Flight Test Program Update (1998), SETP paper](https://man.fas.org/dod-101/sys/ac/docs/f-22-emd-paper.htm)

**Reviewed/access:** Original test-team paper read through a public mirror.

**Use and limit:** Historical flight-test tasks, integrated vehicle subsystem controller and EMD configuration. Prototype/EMD findings must retain their era.


### S30 - [Greeley and Schwartz: F-22 Cockpit Avionics: A Systems Integration Success Story, SPIE 4022 (2000)](https://doi.org/10.1117/12.397775)

**Reviewed/access:** Bibliographic/abstract lead only; publisher full text unavailable.

**Use and limit:** Useful retrieval lead for HMI integration. No finding below depends on an unseen figure or alleged bezel-button map from this paper.


### S31 - [DOT&E FY2024 Annual Report, F-22A modernization section](https://www.dote.osd.mil/Portals/97/pub/reports/FY2024/other/2024Annual-Report.pdf)

**Reviewed/access:** Official indexed Link 16 testing excerpt checked; full report blocked with 403.

**Use and limit:** Link 16 capability/evaluation continues to vary by upgrade. No claim of a universal receive-only or fully fielded transmit configuration.


### S32 - [USAF: F-22 Raptor fact sheet](https://www.af.mil/About-Us/Fact-Sheets/Display/Article/104506/f-22-raptor/About-Us/f-22-raptor/)

**Reviewed/access:** Official indexed specification text checked; page body blocked with 403.

**Use and limit:** Broad fuel/armament cross-check: internal fuel about 8,200 kg; mixed A/G and defensive A/A carriage. Headline figures are not an aerodynamic/engine deck.


### S33 - [DVIDS/USAF: F-22 Raptor Inside the Cockpit (2019)](https://www.dvidshub.net/video/681055/f-22-raptor-inside-cockpit)

**Reviewed/access:** Official video metadata checked in earlier cockpit research; individual frames not analyzed in this pass.

**Use and limit:** Authentic visual follow-up lead. No exact powered symbology, current software, or button semantics inferred from unwatched frames.

reference_sections.heading: S03 - [Lt Col Randy Gordon: F-22 Flight Controls, MIT OpenCourseWare](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/16-687-private-pilot-ground-school-january-iap-2019/resources/special-lecture-f-22-flight-controls/)
reference_sections.text:
**Reviewed/access:** Course record and seven-page slides read; PDF pages 3-5 visually inspected. Video not watched in this pass.

**Use and limit:** FCS synoptic, landing/refueling modes, limiters and pilot-command concepts. Course labeled IAP 2019; slides carry 1/30/20. Teaching material, no production gains.

reference_sections.heading: Local evidence, source snapshots and follow-up leads
reference_sections.text:
- [Source SHA-256 manifest](<C:/Users/Ethans Desktop 2.0/Desktop/DlcBuilder/systems-audit-2026-10-25/source-manifest.json>): exact copied text/source state, Git HEAD and capture timestamp.
- [Frozen Python/Lua suite log](<C:/Users/Ethans Desktop 2.0/Desktop/DlcBuilder/systems-audit-2026-10-25/snapshot-suite.log>): 63/63 checks passed.
- [Audit source snapshot](<C:/Users/Ethans Desktop 2.0/Desktop/DlcBuilder/systems-audit-2026-10-25/source-snapshot>): use this if a current development file has changed since the audit.
- [Downloaded-paper ledger](<C:/Users/Ethans Desktop 2.0/Desktop/DlcBuilder/systems-audit-2026-10-25/references/downloads.json>): successful downloads, hashes and failed retrievals, without pretending failed downloads were inspected.
- [Concurrent source diff](<C:/Users/Ethans Desktop 2.0/Desktop/DlcBuilder/systems-audit-2026-10-25/source-drift.patch>), [finish-state hashes](<C:/Users/Ethans Desktop 2.0/Desktop/DlcBuilder/systems-audit-2026-10-25/source-at-finish.json>) and [report/link verification](<C:/Users/Ethans Desktop 2.0/Desktop/DlcBuilder/systems-audit-2026-10-25/verification.json>).
- [Earlier focused cockpit-layout comparison](<C:/Users/Ethans Desktop 2.0/Desktop/DlcBuilder/cockpit-research-2026-10-25/COCKPIT_LAYOUT_RESEARCH.md>): source-linked screen and stores workflow research, separate from the rejected UI prototypes.
- [Existing broad source catalogue](../../RESOURCES.md) and [historical system audit](../../audit/README.md): useful leads/history, not a fresh verification of every listed source.

**Official photo mirror:** [USAF cockpit photograph and provenance](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Lockheed_Martin_F-22A_Raptor_cockpit.jpg). The copied full image/crops in the cockpit research folder are the same museum photograph, not a claim of a current in-service software capture.

**Selected PDF files used:**

- [Brower chapter](<C:/Users/Ethans Desktop 2.0/Desktop/DlcBuilder/systems-audit-2026-10-25/references/Brower-Avionics-Handbook-Ch32.pdf>), sections listed under S01.
- [MIT F-22 slides](<C:/Users/Ethans Desktop 2.0/Desktop/DlcBuilder/systems-audit-2026-10-25/references/MIT-F22-flight-controls.pdf>), PDF pp. 3-5.
- [USAF CFD paper](<C:/Users/Ethans Desktop 2.0/Desktop/DlcBuilder/systems-audit-2026-10-25/references/Cobalt-USAF-2013-CFD.pdf>), relevant results and release-data limits.
- [NASA historical volume](<C:/Users/Ethans Desktop 2.0/Desktop/DlcBuilder/systems-audit-2026-10-25/references/NASA-Partners-in-Freedom.pdf>), printed pp. 159-165 / PDF pp. 172-178.
- [Hornet guide](<D:/DCS/Mods/aircraft/FA-18C/Doc/DCS FA-18C Early Access Guide EN.pdf>), pages recorded under S14.
- [Viper guide](<C:/Users/Ethans Desktop 2.0/Documents/Codex/2026-10-24/fi/work/gunsight-research/maneuver-cues/DCS-F16C-current-EN.pdf>), pages recorded under S15.
- [Harris/Black author-posted full text](https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Jeffrey-Harris-17/publication/269064311_F-22_control_law_development_and_flying_qualities/links/5693cac008ae3ad8e33b2fbc/F-22-control-law-development-and-flying-qualities.pdf), printed pp. 5-8; read via web, local download unavailable.

This report preserves the existing aircraft source. Findings should be rebased against current work before implementation, especially the actively changing NAV, weapon and display files.

overhaul_coordinated_reading_reports.text:
# F-22 overhaul acceptance campaign

Prepared 27 October 2026. Read-only planning result; no aircraft, mission, installed mod, canonical audit or DCS process was changed. **Every execution result in this campaign is NOT RUN.** Source inspection, extracted reference pages and two rendered reference pages are the evidence produced here. They are not simulator qualification.

The campaign complements the system workstreams by testing complete pilot tasks and transitions. A display selection, successful Lua test, C++ callback, initialized readiness parameter or attractive preview cannot close a flight or native-GPU acceptance item.

## 1. Configuration and evidence contract

### Dated test fixture and project release profile

**ARC-01 owns the single project-wide public-baseline capability/evidence ledger and separate Modernized simulation options.** Its adopted release profile controls WP00 and the mandatory gates. This document proposes **B2014 solely as a dated TEST FIXTURE**: a selected Increment 3.1 and ABOS-equipped, land-based F-22A reference configuration dated 10 April 2014. It is not a competing project baseline or an exact OFP assertion. Every card is parameterized by ARC-01's equipment sheet. B2014 does not assert that every aircraft had that configuration on that date. Record individual capability selections; do not invent a Block/OFP identifier. [R1, R2, R3]

The fixture samples the conventional internal A/A fit, gun, two-internal-GBU-32 A/G fit, Increment 3.1 surface mapping/designation, and installed automatic backup oxygen. It does **not** exhaust the capabilities of Increment 3.1: operational GBU-39 SDB employment is explicitly documented in 2012. If ARC-01 includes SDB, M09-S below is mandatory; a two-GBU-32 sortie cannot qualify a complete Increment 3.1 weapons claim. [R11] The 2022 fact sheet is a later coarse armament/capacity crosscheck; its future-tense modernization prose is not a reliable chronology. The 2001 avionics chapter and 2006 rescue descriptions are dated supporting evidence whose continued applicability must be qualified individually. [R1-R5]

This selected fixture is narrower than the snapshot's offered payload list. Test fixture coverage and Modernized simulation extensions separately:

| Configuration | Treatment |
| --- | --- |
| B2014 internal A/A | Declare the actual DCS AIM-9 and AIM-120 CLSIDs/subtypes used; use a conventional legacy-compatible fit for the first qualification. A generic official weapon-family statement does not establish every subtype. |
| B2014 internal A/G | Declare two stock/native GBU-32 CLSIDs and retained A/A stations. Demonstrate that the released object is the declared guided bomb and accepts the intended target. |
| GBU-39 SDB under the adopted public profile | Add M09-S if included by ARC-01; required for any full Increment 3.1 weapons-capability claim. Verify the exact store/rack and per-store target/release integration; generic bomb classification is insufficient. |
| External ferry tanks | Optional configuration within the public broad aircraft capability; run separate mass, drag, transfer and jettison cases. Do not carry their results into a clean-aircraft curve. |
| Training unguided bomb / CCIP | Explicit **mod training extension**. Useful to verify ballistics and release plumbing; not evidence that B2014 operationally carries that training store. |
| AIM-9X, AIM-120D, AIM-260, MAKO, IRST pod, low-observable tanks | Individually versioned optional configurations; require evidence and host integration appropriate to each. Their presence in the payload/menu is not baseline acceptance. |
| TGP, HMD, HARM/Maverick, naval recovery/ACLS, land autoland, automatic GCAS | Outside the B2014 fixture; ARC-01 must separately adopt/evidence any release option that includes them. Hornet/Viper equipment is not added merely to complete a comparator checklist. Terrain advice can be tested without claiming automatic recovery. |

This scope addresses AV31, AN26, AN30, AS27, AX01/09/10/13/14 and WP00. The selected radar mode names, HOTAS choreography, UI duplication, AFCS limits and timing constants remain named analogue or mod policy unless direct F-22 evidence exists.

### Four labels on every expected result

| Label | Meaning and permitted claim |
| --- | --- |
| **F22-D** | A specific documented F-22 behavior, with source date/configuration. Narrow claim only: for example integrated pitch thrust-vectoring capability, not a recovered scheduling law. |
| **ANALOGUE-H / ANALOGUE-V** | A consciously adopted DCS Hornet or Viper interaction/acceptance idea. It establishes a comparison workflow, not Raptor authenticity. |
| **MOD-P / CODE** | An engineering acceptance budget or the frozen implementation's exact contract. Passing it demonstrates that declared model/UI behavior, not production-aircraft calibration. |
| **UNKNOWN** | Public evidence does not establish the quantity or behavior. Record uncertainty; do not change it to F22-D after a test passes. |

Examples: the snapshot's 180-second ground IRS alignment, illustrative 1 NM/hour uncertainty budget, 60-second continuously qualified APU auto-off, and AFCS engagement envelope are **CODE**. Viper alignment durations and disconnect conditions are **ANALOGUE-V**, not substitutes for those values. Exact production F-22 INS error, approach indexer bands, radar scheduler, detection probability, SAR resolution, weapon LAR and engine deck remain **UNKNOWN** where not documented. [R4, R6-R10; S3-S6]

### Runtime identity is a blocking prerequisite

The frozen text tree is `overhaul/source`, 565 text files, captured **27 October 2026 12:58:25 MDT**. Use its adjacent manifest. Earlier audit JSONs have earlier captures; their line numbers are leads, not current snapshot anchors. The code anchors below were reread in this snapshot.

`coordinated/runtime-baseline.json` is a supplementary observation, not a preserved executable/assets package. It records matching sampled source/installed `bin/f22.dll` hashes (`a1224b2b...524caa`), cockpit EDM (`da19b6bf...5d732`) and external EDM (`1429462f...5d10e`), but **different source/installed default joystick and keyboard hashes**. This must be resolved by identifying the exact package under test and pinning its bindings; no installation was performed in this assignment. The parent reports the locally inspected executable version as **DCS 2.9.30.28738**; verify the actual executable used when running.

Each run must record: DCS executable full path/version/hash; all relevant native DCS DLL identities where adapters are version-sensitive; installed mod path/package manifest and custom DLL hash; cockpit/external model and texture/material bundle identity; source snapshot/commit; default and user `diff.lua` bindings, axis curves, device GUIDs and keyboard layout; mission `.miz` hash and script hashes; map/version; weather/date/time; selected baseline and payload CLSIDs; weight/fuel; start type; GPU/driver/API; screen resolution/FOV or VR runtime/headset/per-eye resolution; graphics options; server/client identity and IC policy if relevant. A change in any material item creates a new run identity and invalidates the dependent comparison, not every unrelated test.

## 2. Fixtures, measurements and pass rules

### Configurable mission kit

Author these missions later in Mission Editor against the identified package. **No `.miz` was created or opened here.** Map/airfield/navaid availability has not been verified. `MAP`, `HOME`, `DIVERT`, `RWY`, runway heading/length/elevation, `ILS_FREQ`, `TCN_CHANNEL/BAND`, and radio presets are mandatory filled fields before the first run. A Caucasus land base can be a candidate, not an assumed working ILS/TACAN installation. Independently check navaid frequency, channel, station position, course reference and runway elevation in the actual build.

Use one home field, one divert, a flat/sea control area, a terrain/landmark area, a segregated surface target area and an A/A target area. Save baseline and perturbation copies; avoid carrying unrelated failures through a case. Use fixed skill, route, altitude, speed, behavior and spawn timing for targets. Combat targets do not maneuver or defend in the first measurement run; add variation only after basic functions pass.

Route geometry is in true local north/east relative to a surveyed origin at HOME: WP1 10 NM north, WP2 10 NM north/20 NM east, WP3 10 NM south/20 NM east, WP4 recovery entry. Add a deliberately behind-ownship point, one crossed-course navaid leg and one fly-by corner. Convert local geometry to actual mission coordinates and record both. DCS world axes are north/up/east in the snapshot bridge (S1); do not silently use magnetic runway heading as true north.

Common nominal fixture, subject to the declared model envelope: daylight, clear weather, no wind, standard pressure/temperature, 50% internal fuel, no external tanks, deterministic payload. Use air starts near 15,000 ft pressure altitude and 350 KCAS for general handling, or the stated task altitude. These are **MOD-P test conditions**, not certified F-22 operating limits. Perturb one factor at a time: heavier fuel, wind, nonstandard pressure/temperature, optional external configuration, night, rain/cloud, sensor fault, utility fault. Log mass and actual conditions rather than relying on a percentage alone.

### Evidence layers and instrumentation

| Layer | Minimum evidence | What it cannot prove |
| --- | --- | --- |
| E0 source/contract | Snapshot anchors; selected unit/fixture results and their exact invocation, toolchain and hashes when executed by the implementation team. | Loaded DLL identity, correct EDM projection, real texture, flight dynamics, host launch/target support. No tests were run here. |
| E1 live cockpit/input/audio | Original screenshot/video with visible run/case/time marker; input press/release log where available; actual sound capture; cockpit and external views. | A picture alone cannot prove sensor freshness, guided flight or force/mass conservation. |
| E2 native/GPU | Live native-ready/reason values, original render-target/GPU observation where available, time/pose-correlated cockpit captures and changing scene evidence. | A nonzero texture or `READY` flag alone cannot establish correct registration, SAR physics, range or target handoff. |
| E3 flight/host | Live EFM/export telemetry, mission event log (shot/hit/death where exposed), observed store count/type and trajectory, start-state/fault timing; track as supplementary evidence. | A replay alone is not a guarantee of the original live result. A simulated C++ aircraft frame is not a DCS flight. |
| E4 fidelity | E1-E3 result plus appropriately applicable F-22 reference and stated comparison uncertainty. | A well-tested estimate remains an estimate. |

Available read-only instrumentation leads: `Radar_Telemetry.lua` explicitly distinguishes changed values from fresh sensor measurements (S7); observation rows require advancing source timestamps (S8). The passive trim hook samples at 0.05-second minimum intervals and checks complete numeric rows, but primarily covers trim/AFCS/airframe data, not the whole vehicle ledger (S9). RAPTOR exports independent suspension WOW, engine units, hydraulic pressure, vector angles, forces and fuel (S1/S2). Native ground-video GPU/timing probes exist (S10). Log actual availability and completeness before using them.

Missing mass-debit, oxygen, audio-onset or server event instrumentation is a **measurement dependency**, not a pass. If a failure cannot be injected through a documented, reproducible mission/host control, keep its E0 fault-injection result and mark the flight case BLOCKED until an observable integration method exists. Do not write cockpit handles to force `READY`, validity, targets, power or damage in a live acceptance run. Diagnostic build perturbations require their own package identity and cannot qualify the unmodified release package.

### Initial engineering budgets

These are proposed **MOD-P** acceptance thresholds for WP00/discipline owners to freeze before execution. They must not be advertised as real-aircraft limits or adjusted after a failed run without a recorded rationale and rerun.

* UI input: one press yields exactly one action; release reaches the original owner even after a page/focus change. No release/fire/dispense resumes after power restoration without the declared fresh-consent action. Input quench is observed within 0.10 s or two measured owner update periods, whichever is greater.
* Numeric entry: invalid/out-of-range text does not change the achieved value; a positive acknowledgement requires readback. The current UFC pending timeout is 1 s; allow one measured UI update for observing the timeout message (S11).
* Basic instrument crosscheck: for stable data with common units/reference, HUD/ADI/telemetry agree within display quantization plus 1 kt, 10 ft and 0.5 degree. Do not apply this between CAS/EAS/TAS, radar/barometric altitude, or true/magnetic headings without conversion.
* AFCS performance: after 15 s settling, hold for 60 s with altitude error <=100 ft and heading/attitude error <=2 degrees in the nominal fixture; no growing oscillation or hidden pilot assistance. Coupled-route cross-track error <=0.2 NM on a straight leg after capture. A declared commanded turn has a separate transient budget. Engagement/disconnect predicates must match the adopted contract exactly.
* Fuel/mass: reconcile start + added - burned - leaked - jettisoned - end quantities. Residual <= max(1 kg, 0.1% of start fuel) over an instrumented five-minute segment, and no unexplained mass step. Separately prove the host mass-change callback and store mass ledger. Round displayed pounds only after comparing SI ledgers.
* Image registration: two independently surveyed scene landmarks at different screen locations agree with the displayed/designated coordinates within 2% of active image width in a nominal static case. Moving-case temporal registration error must fit the measured source refresh interval plus 0.10 s and never use a future pose. A capability owner must freeze a stricter targeting budget before guided-delivery fidelity closure; passing this image test alone does not prove SAR or weapon accuracy.
* Alert lifecycle: no urgent event is silently dropped. Proposed urgent audible/visual onset <=0.5 s from a valid producer condition, with the producer delay and audio scheduling delay measured separately. Any intentional source-specific delay must be separately declared; do not replace historical F-22 sensing delays with this generic presentation budget.
* Regression stability: repeat identical deterministic nominal cases three times; no unexplained count/state differences. Where physics is noisy, report mean/range and the predeclared tolerance, not a blanket bit-for-bit requirement.

Use two independent outcomes: **functional result** PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED/NOT RUN/N/A and **fidelity status** F22-D/ANALOGUE/MOD-P/UNKNOWN. N/A requires a documented configuration exclusion. PARTIAL can describe evidence coverage but does not satisfy a release gate. Failures preserve first evidence and exact reproduction steps; reruns do not erase them.

## 3. Staged mission cards

Each case below is a separate reset/variant unless its steps explicitly test persistence. Every card requires original E1 captures plus the listed evidence. Durations are approximate normal-task time; the full four-condition suite requires additional resets.

### M00 - Identify package, mission and native services (15 min, ground; prerequisite for all)

**Setup:** ground-hot and cold slots at HOME, no active threats, source/installed package manifests, a case/run ID displayed by the mission. Read native service readiness/reasons without forcing them. **Evidence:** E0/E1/E2 and the full runtime identity sheet. **Links:** WP00, WP02, WP10; AX11/12/14, AE17; S1, S10-S14.

| Case | Pilot/operator steps | Measurable pass/fail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NORMAL | Verify actual DCS executable, loaded custom DLL, model/material bundle, active input mappings and `.miz`; open cockpit and native-status pages/logs. | All identities complete; installed inputs intentionally correspond to recorded bindings; zero missing required native services. A self-set readiness constant does not count. |
| LIMIT | Load the same mission/package with the minimum declared rendering configuration and then standard rendering configuration. | The supported package initializes in both; configuration-dependent limits are explicit. Native rejection reason is captured if a version is incompatible. |
| FAILURE | In a separately identified diagnostic/unsupported-version fixture, exercise unavailable native service behavior without bypassing compatibility checks. | No fabricated tracks, image, targeting or launch authorization; clear unavailable status; no crash. This cannot qualify the supported runtime. |
| RECOVERY | Return to the release candidate and reload a fresh slot/mission. | Genuine service readiness returns; diagnostic targets/state do not leak. Package identity matches the recorded candidate. |

**Gate:** presently unpassed, including the known source/installed default-input mismatch. A missing native backend blocks its dependent live claims, even if downstream Lua fixtures pass.

### M01 - Cold, hot and airborne lifecycle (25 min normal cold sortie; M00 required)

**Setup:** three otherwise identical slots: cold ramp, hot ramp, airborne; neutral controls, 50% internal fuel. Add a separate low-reserve ground fixture. **Evidence:** E1/E3 supply/RPM/fuel/actuator/audio timeline. **Links:** WP02/03/10; AV02/14-17/31/35, VT03/05; S2, S5, S15.

| Case | Pilot steps | Measurable pass/fail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NORMAL | Cold: battery, auxiliary power, left then right engine using the modeled separate crank/fuel controls; watch achieved power/pressure; taxi. Repeat hot and air starts without touching switches for 30 s, then move throttles separately. | Each start reaches its declared stable configuration; no double toggle, phantom powered consumer, startup fire/release/CM command or incorrect both-engine throttle coupling. Record elapsed state transitions rather than assuming a brochure start time. |
| LIMIT | Delay the second engine/generator; interrupt one generator during the APU auto-off qualification, then restore. In another ground copy attempt auxiliary start with declared limited battery/SES reserve. | Current CODE continuous 60-second qualification resets when disqualified; reserves cannot be infinite. Failure to model SES is an explicit AV15/26 gap, not evidence that a battery timer authenticates it. |
| FAILURE | Lose one power source; then a separate dual-source outage while a bezel/TDC/trigger/pickle input is held. | Achieved buses/consumers and hydraulic availability match the supply model; held commands quench; no powered door motion solely from an unpowered command. Independent unaffected engine remains controllable. |
| RECOVERY | Restore the surviving supply using the declared controls; reload after the low-reserve test; shut down and respawn. | No stale command replay, free reserve replenishment within the same damaged aircraft, or old failure in the new slot. Canopy hold/lock state is distinguishable from position. |

### M02 - Cockpit, controls, HUD and audio (20 min; M01 normal required)

**Setup:** hot-ramp, then air slot; record default seat/FOV, 2D head positions and device profile. Use a test-only alert producer through an identified supported fixture. **Evidence:** E1 original pixels/audio and input traces; E3 common-unit data. **Links:** WP10/12; AX01/02/09-16, AN06/07/09, NG07/08/10, CG03-09; S1, S11/S12/S16.

| Case | Pilot steps | Measurable pass/fail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NORMAL | Place NAV, tactical, DEF and stores/engine formats on the four displays. Route a format to another screen, focus it, slew; edit a waypoint/QNH through UFC, commit, cancel and read back. Perform 10/30/90-degree banks and heading/counter rollovers in flight. | Correct format/focus acts on the intended owner; source and achieved values meet common-unit budget; no mirroring, inversion, clipping, duplicate labels or blank clickable control claiming success. Current lack of a second radio is recorded rather than covered by a generic COM2 label. |
| LIMIT | Repeat with duplicate formats, maximum-length/invalid numeric entry, minimum/maximum brightness, night lighting, forward/aft/lateral head translations and a held bezel across page change. | Invalid entry changes no achieved value; minimum brightness remains an intensity state; release returns to the original owner; required information is readable at declared supported settings. |
| FAILURE | Hold a control through display power loss; acknowledge fault A while it remains active, then introduce independent B; play an ordinary voice before a new urgent event. | No stuck owner; A acknowledgement is not repair; B demands fresh attention; the urgent event meets the declared presentation budget and identity is retained for both faults. Voice test alone is insufficient. |
| RECOVERY | Restore display power; return format/focus; unmute and reset the alert sources; repeat entry. | No unintended repeated input, erased persistent physical fault or retained hidden mute; display/control state follows the declared reset/persistence policy. |

### M03 - Navigation, UFC transactions and independent recovery sensors (25 min; M01/M02 required)

**Setup:** cardinal route and behind-ownship point; verified HOME/DIVERT navaids; no wind baseline and a crosswind copy. **Evidence:** E1/E3 true/magnetic references, position, selected source, quality, station bearing/range and approach receiver flags. **Links:** WP04/10; AN01-13/19-21/27-29, NG01-04/07-10, AX03/04/06-08; S3/S4/S6/S11/S17.

| Case | Pilot steps | Measurable pass/fail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NORMAL | Align from cold; enter/verify a route coordinate, elevation and course; select north/east/behind points; fly a leg and navaid crossing. Tune ILS independently of waypoint steering and GPS aiding. | Source, reference and units remain explicit; range/bearing agree with surveyed geometry; behind/off-FOV conformal cue hides while usable numeric data remains. Receiver guidance corresponds to the tuned signal, not the INS runway position. |
| LIMIT | Fly route in crosswind; change QNH, true/magnetic display reference, course and steering source separately; attempt invalid coordinate/channel/frequency. | Ground track/heading differ consistently; each setting changes only its intended quantity. TACAN angular CDI/station datum meets the adopted contract; invalid tuning gives rejection/unavailable response. |
| FAILURE | Disable GPS aiding through the declared control; later remove one navigation receiver or power supply in separate copies. Fly with a valid ILS and degraded inertial estimate. | Quality and position behavior match the declared INS model; do not claim realistic random drift from the illustrative uncertainty budget. Loss of INS does not delete independently valid received ILS. Unavailable bearing/range is flagged, not replaced with truth. |
| RECOVERY | Restore aiding, perform an adopted position fix if implemented, retune a verified receiver and go around once. | No discontinuous unexplained route/target jump, silently overwritten waypoint elevation or false perfect alignment. Current ground 180 s / eligible aided air-recovery 30 s contracts are measured as CODE, not taken from Viper timings. |

### M04 - AFCS, pilot override and land recovery (30 min; M03 and M05 basic envelope required)

**Setup:** straight leg, fly-by turn, navaid radial, approach and missed-approach route; clear first, then wind/low-visibility variants; clean and heavier-fuel copies. **Evidence:** E1/E3 AP active/reason/axis/override, captured versus selected references, pilot axes, throttle ownership, path and touchdown data. **Links:** WP04/05; AN03-05/14-26/30, NG05/06/09, VG05, PF06/16-18; S2/S3/S18.

| Case | Pilot steps | Measurable pass/fail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NORMAL | Capture ATT and barometric hold; engage heading then route steering. Demonstrate any separately declared speed/AoA throttle assist. Disconnect deliberately; fly manual ILS, go around, then land. | Nominal hold budgets pass with no pilot correction; cockpit mode matches actual controlled axes. ILS is manual received guidance. Heavier approach at equal adopted AoA/configuration needs higher dynamic pressure; no fixed-speed substitution. |
| LIMIT | Test one point inside and outside each current engagement bound and stale NAV guidance; separate ATT stick recapture, CPL temporary override and paddle disconnect. | Exact adopted eligibility/rejection/reason and axis ownership match the contract. Current bounds in `Autopilot.h:56` are CODE, not Viper or F-22 flight limits. No hidden ALT-hold climb during roll-only NAV. |
| FAILURE | Remove a guidance source while coupled, then separately electrical/control availability; test rejected A/T engagement and automatic A/T loss on approach. | Safe mode transition/disconnect is observable; pilot control available; timed annunciation distinguishes failed engagement from existing engagement loss. No runway-coordinate autoland inference from ILS. |
| RECOVERY | Recover manually, restore source, explicitly re-engage, perform missed approach and second landing. | No uncommanded re-engagement, old throttle hold or reference jump. Measured touchdown/rollout remains within the scenario runway; record performance rather than claiming a published stopping distance. |

Normal 12-degree and historical single-engine 11.5-degree approach references have an EMD anchor; applying exact bands/laws to B2014 is still a declared estimate. Carrier CASE/ACLS tests and automatic terrain escape remain optional, separately justified branches. [R6]

### M05 - Propulsion, fuel, utilities and physical consistency (30 min nominal; M01/M02 required)

**Setup:** repeatable cruise/acceleration/approach conditions; 25/50/90% fuel copies; clean first, external-tank/door/gear variants separately; tanker only after normal handling passes. **Evidence:** E1/E3 20 Hz or better flight dynamics where available, model-step/event capture for short transients, fuel/mass ledger, core RPM/temperature/flow, engine force and achieved surface/vector state. **Links:** WP01-03; PF01-22, AV01/03-13/18-30/33-37, VG01-12, VT01/02/04/05; S1/S2/S15/S18.

| Case | Pilot steps | Measurable pass/fail |
| --- | --- | --- |

N/A exclusions and BLOCKED items are visible. |

**Profile-sensitive gates:** G0 uses ARC-01's authoritative release ledger, not B2014 as a project baseline. Selecting different weapon generations/equipment changes G4/M06-M07 and G5/M08-M09/SDB requirements. Selecting EOS versus ABOS changes G6/M10's oxygen response. Selecting a different documented display/CNI/AFCS capability changes the applicable G2/G3/M02-M04 tasks. VR/MP claims activate the relevant G7 hardware/deployment cases; Modernized simulation options add separately identified variants rather than silently expanding F22-D claims. G8 closes only the advertised selected profile, with all exclusions explicit. Generic numeric budgets remain MOD-P under every profile.

Practical execution order: **M00 -> M01 -> M02 -> M05 basic envelope -> M03 -> M04 -> M06 -> M07 -> M08 -> M09 -> M10 -> M11 -> M12**. M05's extended envelope/thermal/tanker variants continue as their dependencies become available. Parallel engineering work can prepare fixtures/results, but no flight is gated by a test result from a different package.

Budget approximately **six hours for one nominal pass of the cards**, and **10-14 pilot/operator hours** for planned four-condition variants, resets and three-run deterministic spot repeats, excluding defect investigation and a full performance envelope. Split it into four sessions: (1) identity/ground/interface/NAV, (2) vehicle/AFCS/recovery, (3) A/A/EW and surface/weapon chains, (4) coupled faults/MP/VR/rehearsal. A 25-minute smoke selection may support iteration, but cannot substitute for this release campaign.

For a UI-only change, repeat its M02/M03/M08 interaction and the corresponding held-input/power-loss regression. For radar or target/weapon changes, repeat M06-M09 plus M11 donor/peer/source transitions. For EFM/power/fuel changes, repeat M01/M04/M05/M10 and M12. For a custom DLL, DCS native DLL/build, GPU renderer, EDM/material or input-package change, reopen M00 and all affected native/display/input gates; choose reruns from the actual dependency, not a blanket old green test suite.

Per-case record template: `run_id, case_id, package/mission hashes, baseline/options, setup/initial state, expected label and budget, prerequisites, exact pilot steps, actual values/timestamps, evidence paths, functional result, fidelity status, audit IDs, defect ID, reviewer, rerun linkage`. Store screenshots/video/CSV/event logs together under that run. Mission scoring is a summary of independently checked conditions, not the acceptance oracle; an aircraft script must not validate itself solely by reading its own success flag.

# F-22 overhaul: integration architecture, native feasibility and proof gates

Planning assignment B. Read-only review, 27 October 2026. This document proposes work; it does not change the aircraft, installed mod, canonical audit or any mission, and it does not report a new DCS test. No aircraft build or test suite was executed for this assignment. Existing test code was inspected. Source anchors below are relative to the immutable `overhaul/source/` text snapshot, not the live checkout.

## 1. Decision and baseline

Make command identity, publication contracts, lifecycle and build identity release-blocking foundations before adding equipment. The current split between owned Lua policy, the EFM and shared native devices is workable. It should be formalized, not replaced by a union of Viper and Hornet equipment. Most physical utilities, cockpit transactions and degraded behavior can be implemented with owned C++/Lua state. Native radar, received radio messages, weapon internals and renderer callbacks use a materially more fragile integration tier.

The 565-text-file snapshot was captured at **2026-10-27 12:58:25 MDT / 18:58:25 UTC**. Its adjacent manifest is the source identity. Root's `source-drift.json` reported zero textual drift when supplied to this assignment. That says nothing about binary provenance, live memory, mission state or flight acceptance.
